FOUR ALTERNATIVES. FOUR DIFFERENT REASONS.

Sesami alternatives.
Compare the implementation, too.

Sesami is worth evaluating as a retail booking platform with an API, SDK and resource model. Small includes five resources; Pro adds groups and Klaviyo with twenty resources; Premium lists forty resources and multi-location. A lower app subscription does not automatically replace a custom implementation.

What would make switching worthwhile?

Sesami may be the right choice when your agency needs its SDK or your retail operation values its resource model. A lower subscription does not automatically replace a custom implementation.

YOUR DECISION STARTS HERE

The differences that matter for Sesami users.

01

A custom storefront

Sesami Small at $19/month lists API/SDK access. Cowlendar’s public API is beta and has a defined endpoint set; compare the actual technical requirement.

02

Groups and lifecycle marketing

Sesami Pro is $129/month and lists group appointments, Klaviyo and reports. These are different requirements from basic appointment booking.

03

Multiple retail locations

Premium is $299/month and lists multi-location with forty resources. Include implementation, resource mapping and staff operations in the decision.

YOUR MIGRATION CHECKLIST

Test the reason you are switching.

  1. Inventory the custom work List the theme changes, SDK usage, endpoints and automation events the existing installation depends on.
  2. Map resources to the new setup Confirm how people, rooms or counters translate into the alternative app. Do not compare unrelated resource counts as if they were identical.
  3. Budget the transition Allow for implementation and acceptance testing as well as the monthly subscription. Reconcile future bookings before switching the storefront.

Sesami alternatives: common questions.

Does Sesami offer a free plan for a live store?

The free tier in the checked listing is for development stores. Small starts at $19/month for a live-store feature set.

Can Cowlendar replace a Sesami SDK implementation?

Not automatically. Compare the required custom interface and API endpoints. Cowlendar’s beta public API supports defined booking operations, which may not match a storefront built around another vendor’s SDK.
